member.name: T:Country_PackageAPI.Authorization.CountryRoleRequirement
member.summary: "Does the caller hold for the resource's country (and, when specified, org level)?" The coarse-grained, resource-based check the API layer is expected to run before invoking Application (see IApprovalWorkflowService's remarks and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4.2). It is deliberately coarse: step-instance-specific rules ("only the named approver may decide this step") stay in the Domain, and the "does the person being *named* as approver currently hold clearance" check stays in Application, because neither can be expressed against the caller's own principal alone.

member.name: T:Country_PackageAPI.Auth.DevHeaderAuthenticationHandler
member.summary:
Stand-in for Microsoft Entra ID in this exercise: identity is established from an X-User-Id header carrying a seeded 's GUID, instead of validating a real OIDC bearer token. This is deliberately the *only* place in the solution that knows about that header - everywhere else deals in ClaimsPrincipal/Guid the same way it would with real Entra ID tokens. Swapping to Entra ID in the Azure target architecture (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6.3) means replacing the scheme registration in Program.cs with AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi - nothing downstream of authentication (authorization handlers, controllers, Application/Domain) changes, because none of it reads this header directly; it only ever reads off the principal.
This handler ONLY establishes identity. It never queries roles/clearance - that is always re-read from UserCountryRole by the resource-based authorization handlers and, defensively, by the Application layer itself (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4.1).

member.name: T:Country_PackageAPI.Middleware.ExceptionHandlingMiddleware
member.summary: The single place that translates a thrown into an HTTP response, so controllers stay free of try/catch and status-code bookkeeping. Every response is a standard body (RFC 9457) carrying the request's trace id for correlation with logs - see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §7 "Observability". Unrecognized exceptions are logged with full detail but returned to the caller as a generic 500 with no internal detail, since a stack trace or exception message can leak information about operational data or infrastructure the caller should never see.
